preliminary_answers: WTI at Cushing, Oklahoma: the daily spot quote for physical crude changing hands now; distinct from the May futures settlement.
20 April 2020, minus $36.98 per barrel, for one trading day; positive $8.91 on 21 April.
Attributed to pandemic demand collapse, filling Cushing storage and the May futures contract expiring 21 April, forcing holders unable to take delivery to sell to scarce buyers.
A seller pays a buyer to accept barrels; the buyer must have capacity to receive or store them. The story supplies no actual transaction example or detailed settlement mechanics.
The charted negative observation was WTI-specific; Brent stayed positive. Both benchmarks suffered a shared slump. Two benchmarks cannot establish the complete extent across all oil markets.

WTI rebounded positive next day and rose to $35.57 by 29 May; Brent and WTI approached $40 late June. Expiry-specific pressure plausibly explains brevity, but the prose does not explain the later recovery or why next-day capacity conditions differed.

The prices establish timing, magnitude, benchmark contrast and positive weekly/monthly averages. Prose attributes causation to EIA and says the data do not test it. Spot/futures transmission, measured storage constraints, other contributors, complete market coverage and recovery causes remain unanswered.
